title: Document structure
description: <document folder>/structure.json, schema 1.0 -- the sections of a Convention d'utilisation (CU) or a Base de projet (BP): which there are, in which order, how deep, and whether each is printed (calc/structure.py). Written by Woodcore whole, in one shape (fixed key order, two-space indent), and read by calc/structure.py alone; the document's entry .typ has a block of `#heading` and `#include` lines generated from it between the tags `// woodcore:structure` and `// woodcore:/structure` (structure.sync_entry). The report (RS) has no such file: its order and enabled state stay in its own #include lines. A node is a GROUP (`title` in three languages and `children`, no file) or a LEAF (`file` `Sections/<id>.typ`, no title and no children): one lowest-level section is one file. The tree goes four levels deep, which this schema states by nesting the same shape four times -- the walker has no $ref. Every rule it cannot express -- the id's shape, an id unique in its document, a leaf's file named after its id, a group or a leaf and never both, no key it does not know -- is checked by structure.check_source.

schema_version.description: -- pinned: a file written at another version is refused rather than read as this one.

format.description: What this file is, so a structure.json that is something else is refused by name.

document.description: Which document this structure belongs to. The report (rs) has none.

headings.description: `absolute` where the document writes its headings at the level they are printed at and gives each chapter a file of its own, `Sections/<chapter id>.typ` (the engineer's request of 06.10.2026); absent, the document is laid out with offsets, as until then. Optional and additive, so schema_version stays 1.0.

sections.description: The document's top-level sections, in print order. An empty list is a document with nothing in it yet.

id.description: The section's id: English, lower case, letters and digits parted by single hyphens, starting with a letter -- `^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*$` (checked by structure.check_source, which the walker below cannot express). Unique in the document, and **never changed by a rename**: it names the section's file (`Sections/<id>.typ`) and everything that refers to the section.

title.description: A GROUP's title, in the three languages -- it is printed as a heading in the document's own language. A leaf states none: its title is the first heading of its file, and a second place for it would drift.

file.description: A LEAF's file, `Sections/<id>.typ`, relative to the document's folder: one lowest-level section is one file, named after its id, with no number prefix. A leaf has no children.

enabled.description: Whether the section is printed. Default true. A disabled section keeps its file and is written into the entry as `// disabled: <id> (<file>)`; a disabled group takes its whole subtree out with it.

shared_with.description: A LEAF's: the other documents its file is shared with. The file is the unit of sharing; what stays synchronised is only what lies between the `woodcore:shared` tags inside it. Maintained by Woodcore's share and stop-sharing, and reconciled against the tags of the copies when the structure is read.

children.description: A GROUP's sections, in print order. A group has children and no file; it prints its title as a heading of its own depth, and its leaves are included one level down.

enabled.description: Whether the section is printed, as above.

shared_with.description: A leaf's: the other documents it is shared with, as above.

enabled.description: Whether the section is printed, as above.

shared_with.description: A leaf's: the other documents it is shared with, as above.

enabled.description: Whether the section is printed, as above.

shared_with.description: A leaf's: the other documents it is shared with, as above.

children.description: A group at the deepest level holds nothing: the structure goes down four levels and no further (structure.check_source refuses a fifth).
